title: Publisher Mutual Claims Desk
persona: Publisher Mutual - a fictional Australian general insurer handling home, motor and small commercial property claims
tagline: A claims workbench where coverage answers are cited, decisions are trust-scored, and exceptions surface before a cheque goes out.
elevatorPitch: A claims handler opens a claim and gets its documents read, the coverage question answered against the actual policy wording with the clause cited, a payable / not-payable call with a live REMi trust score, and any integrity exception flagged - all grounded in the claim file, never invented.

archetype.name: Claims workbench
archetype.demonstrates: A live claims queue on the left and a reading-room workbench on the right: select a claim, then intake extraction, coverage Q&A, a trust-scored decision and an exception check all operate on that claim's real documents.

theme.mood: a calm, authoritative marine-blue claims desk - deep Progress Agentic RAG blue as the structural field, a single warm amber accent used sparingly for guidance and status, the real claim documents rendered as bright paper objects against the navy chrome

surfaces.label: Claims Desk
surfaces.tagline: The live claims queue and where every claim stands today.
surfaces.sells: The whole book of work on one screen - volumes, cycle time and the claims that need a decision now.

surfaces.label: Claim Intake
surfaces.tagline: Read a submitted claim's documents into structured intake fields.
surfaces.sells: Unstructured paperwork - a First Notice of Loss, a policy schedule - turned into clean, structured claim fields the handler can act on, extracted by ARAG, not re-keyed by hand.

surfaces.label: Coverage Q&A
surfaces.tagline: Ask a coverage question, get a cited answer from the policy wording.
surfaces.sells: The question a claims handler asks a dozen times a day - is this covered - answered against the actual Product Disclosure Statement, with the clause cited and clickable, never a confident guess.

surfaces.label: Coverage Decision
surfaces.tagline: Payable, not payable or needs-more-info - cited, and REMi-scored.
surfaces.sells: A defensible coverage call with its reasons cited AND a live REMi trust score - so a low-confidence decision is caught before a cheque goes out, not after.

surfaces.label: Exception Check
surfaces.tagline: Cross-check the claim against the policy and integrity indicators.
surfaces.sells: The inconsistencies a busy handler misses - a date that doesn't match the police report, a premium in arrears at the loss date, a claim over a sub-limit - surfaced with the source, before settlement.

surfaces.label: Portfolio
surfaces.tagline: Claim volumes, cycle time, status mix and peril breakdown as charts.
surfaces.sells: A claims manager's own book of work as charts - where the backlog is, what is slow, which perils are driving cost.

surfaces.label: Claims Copilot
surfaces.tagline: ARAG's own Retrieval Agent plans across live policy and claims-history systems.
surfaces.sells: The agentic story done for real: ARAG's own Retrieval Agent - not our code - plans, calls this app's live policy, claimant-history and prior-claims tools over MCP, and answers only from what it actually retrieved, streamed live so the room watches it think.

surfaces.label: Underwriting Risk Summary
surfaces.tagline: Synthesise an application, inspection report and risk data into a cited risk summary.
surfaces.sells: A structured risk rating, the specific risk factors and a recommended underwriting action - synthesised by ARAG from the application form, an independent inspection and the risk-data feed, never guessed from the product line alone.

surfaces.label: Broker Copilot
surfaces.tagline: Natural-language Q&A over products, rates and compliance bulletins for the broker channel.
surfaces.sells: The question a broker asks between quotes - what does this product cover, what loading applies, what must I disclose - answered against Publisher's own product sheets, rate card and compliance bulletins, cited and never a claim file.

architectureFlow.detail: The claims workbench UI - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
Express server holds the KB service-account token server-side and proxies every ARAG call.
Grounded, streamed answer generation over the claim file - every claim traces to a cited paragraph.
Query-time structured-JSON extraction - reads a claim document into typed intake fields.
Real RAG-triad scoring (groundedness / answer relevance / context relevance), authenticated by the KB service-account token.
ARAG's own Retrieval Agent plans and calls back OUT to this app's MCP tools (JWT forwarded so the app's RBAC applies) - ARAG is the agent, not a homegrown planner.
Citations, structured fields and scores render through truthful-by-construction components - never hand-typed.

/.detail: The claims desk UI - the live queue and today's KPIs.
Holds the KB service-account token server-side; the browser never sees it.
Live document counts and the current claim files come straight from the KB.
The book-of-work volumes are a clearly-labelled synthetic portfolio (the 8 detailed claims are the live queue) - computed on screen, never a hand-typed headline number.
The queue, KPIs and activity feed render from real, computed values.

/intake.detail: The claim intake view - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
Proxies the extraction call with the KB service-account token server-side.

ARAG reads the claim's own First Notice of Loss and policy schedule and returns typed intake fields (claimant, policy, peril, date of loss, amount) as schema-conformant JSON, grounded in the document.
The structured fields render as a generative-UI card, with the source document it grounded on one click away.

/coverage.detail: The coverage Q&A view - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
Holds the KB service-account token server-side and proxies the ask.
Grounded, streamed answer over the policy wording and the claim file - every claim traces to a cited clause.
Real RAG-triad score on the answer, against the full retrieved context.
The cited clause is clickable and opens the actual source document at that record.

/decision.detail: The coverage-decision view - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
Holds the KB service-account token server-side and proxies the ask.
A payable / not-payable / needs-more-info determination reasoned only from the policy wording and the claim file, with each reason cited.
Real RAG-triad trust score - a low-confidence decision is flagged for review, never shown as settled.
The verdict, its cited reasons and the live trust score render as one unit.

/exceptions.detail: The exception-check view - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
Holds the KB service-account token server-side and proxies the ask.
Cross-checks the claim against the policy schedule and the claims integrity-indicators reference, citing every inconsistency it finds.
Each exception renders with the source that evidences it, one click from the record.

/reports.detail: The claims-insight dashboard - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
The live document count comes from the KB via the server proxy.

/reports.stage: ARAG extracts insight from each documented claim's files
/reports.detail: A query-time answer_json_schema grounded-answer call (the working structured-JSON path Claim Intake uses) reads each documented claim's First Notice of Loss narrative, adjuster report and decision letter, scoped by claim_number, and pulls out the cause-of-loss theme, claimant sentiment, integrity signals and coverage complexity - dimensions no coded claim field carries. Verified live (scripts/extract-insight.mjs).
The dashboard charts exactly the claims that extraction genuinely covered - the documented desk claims. The wider seeded book has no documents to extract from and is never charted as 'extracted'.
The per-claim extracted fields and the summary charts are drawn from the real extraction to the dataviz standard.

/copilot.detail: The Claims Copilot view - streams the agent's live NDJSON trace as it plans, calls tools and composes.
Relays ARAG's own Retrieval Agent trace and applies the honest-refusal gate; it never calls the tools itself and never substitutes a homegrown planner.

get_policy_status, get_claimant_history and get_claim reach the insurer's live systems; search_claim_documents runs a scoped semantic-retrieval call over the KB's policy and claim documents. Each dispatches through the app's own handlers (JWT forwarded so its RBAC applies).

/copilot.stage: ARAG Retrieval Agent plans and calls /mcp
/copilot.detail: A mode:'agent' KB (a Smart Agent over an MCP context node) drives the tools over this app's live /mcp endpoint - blending STRUCTURED live data with UNSTRUCTURED document retrieval in a single reasoning loop.
The agent composes one answer from both the live tool results and the retrieved policy/claim documents; the surface shows BOTH - the tool trail AND the knowledge-box sources it grounded on.

/underwriting.detail: The underwriting desk - selects an application, never calls ARAG directly.
Holds the KB service-account token server-side and proxies the synthesis.
The working query-time structured-JSON path - NOT the broken ingest-time DA Generator task - scoped to this application's own documents via the application_number label.
A typed risk rating, key risk factors and a recommended action, grounded in the application, inspection and risk-data triad.
Each source document is clickable and opens at the real record.

/broker-copilot.detail: The broker copilot view - never calls ARAG directly, never holds a token.
Holds the KB service-account token server-side and proxies the ask.
Grounded, streamed answer scoped to product sheets, the rate card and compliance bulletins via a doc_type filter_expression - never a claim file or application.
Real RAG-triad score on the answer, against the full retrieved context.
The cited product, rate or compliance fact is clickable and opens the actual source document.

pageContext.whatItDoes: This app calls ARAG server-side for document extraction, grounded retrieval, generation and quality scoring - the browser never talks to ARAG directly.
pageContext.value: Every claim answer is either a genuine ARAG mechanism at work or an honestly disclosed synthetic dataset - never a hardcoded answer dressed up as one.

/.whatItDoes: The claims desk aggregates the live queue of claim files, the current document count from the KB, and a synthetic book-of-work portfolio into one view - the queue and counts are live, the portfolio volumes are clearly-labelled demo data.
/.value: A claims manager sees where the whole book stands in the first five seconds - what is waiting on a decision, what is slow - without opening ten files.

/intake.whatItDoes: You pick a claim and ARAG reads its own submitted documents - the First Notice of Loss and the policy schedule - and returns the intake fields as structured, typed JSON, grounded in the document it read.
/intake.value: The re-keying that starts every claim - claimant, policy number, peril, date of loss, estimated amount - is done from the paperwork itself in seconds, with the source one click away, instead of typed in by hand.

/coverage.whatItDoes: You ask a coverage question in plain language. The app proxy sends it to ARAG's grounded-answer call, which retrieves the relevant policy wording and claim documents, generates a cited answer, and scores it with REMi before it is shown.
/coverage.value: The question every claim turns on - is this covered - is answered against the actual policy wording, with the clause cited and clickable, so a handler acts on the document, not a memory of it.

/decision.whatItDoes: The app frames the coverage call for the selected claim and asks ARAG for a payable / not-payable / needs-more-info determination reasoned only from the policy and the claim file, each reason cited, then REMi-scores the answer.
/decision.value: A defensible decision with its reasons cited and a live trust score attached - so a low-confidence call is caught and reviewed before money moves, not queried in a complaint later.

/exceptions.whatItDoes: The app asks ARAG to cross-check the selected claim against its policy schedule and Publisher's claims integrity-indicators reference, and to cite every inconsistency it finds.
/exceptions.value: The quiet risks a busy handler misses - a date-of-loss that doesn't match the police report, a premium in arrears at the loss date, an amount over a sub-limit - are surfaced with their evidence, before settlement.

/reports.whatItDoes: Every value on this page is a real ARAG extraction: a query-time answer_json_schema grounded-answer call reads each documented claim's FNOL narrative, adjuster report and decision letter and pulls out the cause theme, the claimant's tone, the integrity signals and the coverage complexity - dimensions no coded claim field carries. Scoped to the claims genuinely extracted, shown per claim, not asserted.
/reports.value: Proves the product's core move end to end - unstructured documents in, structured chartable fields out. A claims manager sees the themes, sentiment and risk signals that only reading every file reveals, and can see per claim exactly what ARAG read out of it.

/copilot.whatItDoes: ARAG's own Retrieval Agent plans a check, then calls this app's MCP tools - the structured live systems (policy master, claims-history register, claim record) AND a knowledge-box search over the unstructured policy and claim documents - and blends both into one grounded answer. The trace, the live tool calls and the knowledge-box documents it grounded on are all shown live.
/copilot.value: The differentiated ARAG story: one agent reasoning across live operational systems AND the document corpus together - 'the premium was in arrears [live data] and here is the clause that lets us reduce the claim [policy wording]' - not document Q&A with a separate data lookup bolted on.

/underwriting.whatItDoes: You pick an application from the underwriting desk and run the synthesis. The app proxy sends a query-time structured request to ARAG scoped to that application's own documents, and ARAG returns a typed risk rating, risk factors and a recommended action grounded in the application form, the inspection report and the risk-data feed.
/underwriting.value: A new-business risk call that would take an underwriter ten minutes of cross-referencing three separate documents is synthesised in seconds, with every factor traceable to its source - never a guess from the product line or the applicant's name alone.

/broker-copilot.whatItDoes: You ask a product, rating or compliance question in plain language. The app proxy sends it to ARAG's grounded-answer call, scoped to the broker product sheets, rate card and compliance bulletins only, which retrieves the relevant wording, generates a cited answer, and scores it with REMi before it is shown.
/broker-copilot.value: The question a broker asks between quotes - what's covered, what loading applies, what must I disclose - answered against Publisher's actual current product and compliance material, with the fact cited and clickable, so a broker never relies on memory of a rate that may have changed.

researchPhase.note: research/publisher-claims.md - general-insurance claims terminology, workflow, document types, roles and edge cases. Corpus built from it.

safety.disclaimer: Demonstration data - Publisher Mutual is a fictional general insurer and every claim, claimant, policy, document and figure is synthetic. Not insurance, financial or legal advice.

answerable: Is sudden water damage from a burst flexible hose covered under the TideProtect Home and Contents policy?
Is the Delacroix flood claim payable given their policy schedule?
What excess applies to a windscreen claim when the Glass Excess Waiver endorsement is held?
Does the Tomas Ruiz theft claim have any inconsistencies a handler should flag?
What loading applies to a driver under 25 with a modified vehicle under TideDrive Motor?
Does the Southbank Import Traders warehouse application need underwriting referral given its aerosol stock and lack of sprinklers?
refusal: What is the current RBA cash rate target?
Draft a United States Medicare appeal letter for a hospital claim.

personas.note: The claims-desk narrative is decision governance and defensible, trust-scored answers with data staying in the insurer's own environment - a CIO's risk/governance register. The architecture reveal, the RBAC-carried agent-over-MCP Copilot and the honest disclosed-gap framing map to the Solutions Architect. Developer/builder considered and set aside: the story here is a claims operation's risk, not an embed/integration build.
